cases.naive_gap: +0.96 in favour of PoisonedRAG, read as though corpus poisoning does not work
cases.numeric_consequence: The apparent gap is between an answer-manipulation rate and a baseline evaluated on that same metric, so it is internally valid but does not transport: the same attack on the same dataset and retriever is recorded at 0.01 by PoisonedRAG and at 84.2-99.4 by its own authors, because the outcome unit differs. No coordinate-matched cross-paper number exists.
cases.numeric_consequence_short: C4 differs: 0.01 scores answer manipulation, 84.2 scores top-20 retrieval, so no gap is defined.

cases.numeric_consequence: gap +3.7% -> -45.3%; ranking reverses at matched budget, but C4 (different objectives) makes the comparison undefined
cases.numeric_consequence_short: No matched operating point exists for C4 (targeted answer vs refusal), so no gap is defined at any budget.

cases.naive_gap: The reading a reader forms: a defense reduces poisoning attack success to <=15%, from a starting point RobustRAG states as 'over 90%' and a reader supplies from PoisonedRAG's headline 0.97. RobustRAG transports no 0.97, and its own vanilla poisoning rates are 37.0-86.0.
cases.naive_gap_short: Defense credited with reducing poisoning ASR to <=15%
cases.numeric_consequence: No cross-harness gap is defined: the attack instantiations differ (C2), the corpora and retrievers differ (C1), and a certified accuracy is not an empirical ASR (C4). The recoverable statement is within-harness only. The 'over 90%' summary is a maximum over a union of two attacks whose vanilla ASR ranges are disjoint.
cases.numeric_consequence_short: No number is transported; RobustRAG re-implements the attack, and its own poisoning ASRs are 37-86.

cases.numeric_consequence: gap +1.2% is uninterpretable; different objectives (DoS vs targeted answer) preclude ranking
cases.numeric_consequence_short: Objectives differ (denial of service vs targeted answer), so the 1.2-point gap does not rank the two attacks.

cases.numeric_consequence: gap +66.66% survives on MedSquad at matched budget; but domain transfer (NQ vs MedSquad) limits generalizability
cases.numeric_consequence_short: At five injected documents on MedSquad the 66.66-point gap stands; it does not transfer to NQ.
All five coordinates match, so the 6.9-point gap stands as reported.

cases.numeric_consequence: gap +6.9 points has unknown sign after controlling for backbone/retriever difference
cases.numeric_consequence_short: Backbone and retriever differ, so the 6.9-point gap has no determined sign.

cases.naive_gap: +4.53 accuracy/EM in favor of RGB's ChatGPT
cases.naive_gap_short: +4.53 accuracy/EM in favor of RGB's ChatGPT
cases.numeric_consequence: gap +4.53 has unknown sign: substring accuracy >= strict EM, so RGB's advantage partly or wholly reflects metric leniency
cases.numeric_consequence_short: Substring accuracy is weaker than exact match, so the 4.53-point gap has no determined sign.

cases.numeric_consequence: improvements +7.55 vs +1.68 are incomparable: ChainOfNote's baseline (34.28) operates without gold context vs RAAT's baseline (85.47) with gold
cases.numeric_consequence_short: The two baselines differ in whether gold context is present, so the two gains are not commensurable.

cases.naive_gap: +4.4 accuracy in favor of ASTUTE RAG
cases.naive_gap_short: +4.4 accuracy in favor of ASTUTE RAG
cases.numeric_consequence: gap +4.4 points -> unchanged; coordinates match for accuracy comparison
cases.numeric_consequence_short: Model, dataset, retrieval and metric match, so the 4.4-point accuracy gap stands.

cases.numeric_consequence: response-level F1 78.7% cannot be compared to span-level metrics; C4 granularity mismatch
cases.numeric_consequence_short: Response-level and span-level scores are different units, so the contrast holds only within one unit.

cases.numeric_consequence: gap 81.7% vs 47.5% conflates aggregate vs single-task, different conflict types, and different models; no matched comparison recoverable
cases.numeric_consequence_short: Aggregate and single-task scores under different conflict types and models cannot be differenced.

cases.numeric_consequence: gap +23.9 points -> unchanged; within-paper controlled experiment
cases.numeric_consequence_short: Within one paper and one harness the 23.9-point gap stands as reported.

cases.numeric_consequence: gap +4.0 points -> unchanged; properly controlled comparison
cases.numeric_consequence_short: Within one paper and one harness the 4.0-point gap stands as reported.

cases.numeric_consequence: gap +16.75 confounds harder test subset + stricter metric for ADAPT-LLM; true method difference is unknown
cases.numeric_consequence_short: A harder test subset and a stricter metric are confounded with the method, so 16.75 is not a method effect.

correction_note: An earlier coding of this entry attributed the string 'from 97%' to RobustRAG and treated the case as a transported attack rate. RobustRAG writes 'from over 90%', attributes the 90+% figure to prompt injection rather than to PoisonedRAG, and re-implements the poisoning attack rather than quoting it. The '97' that does appear in RobustRAG (L1502) is its own prompt-injection ASR for Llama2-C7B on RQA, not PoisonedRAG's 0.97. The verdict changes from 'narrows' to 'undefined'.
headline: Of 8 cross-paper comparisons an author actually stated, 4 are undefined, 2 narrow to a matched operating point, and 2 survive unchanged; the further 4 survey-invited juxtapositions are comparisons no author made.
